explanation: Indonesians traditionally regard the feet as the lowest and least respectful part of the body, so showing the soles of your feet to someone, resting your feet on furniture, or pointing your feet at a person is seen as disrespectful. The custom is rooted in broader Islamic and Southeast Asian etiquette around keeping feet out of view in social settings. It's treated as a genuine breach of manners rather than a minor slip.
local_tip: Sit with your feet flat on the floor or with knees stacked rather than ankle-over-knee, and never rest your feet on tables or chairs.

also_check.note: The feet are the lowest body part; pointing the soles at someone or touching them with a foot is deeply offensive.
Showing the soles of your feet is a serious insult, as feet are seen as unclean.
Pointing feet at someone or at religious objects is considered poor manners, though less severe than in Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Indonesian Etiquette: How You Can Avoid Causing Offense
